description: Standard-cell geometry from its height in TRACKS: height, area, tracks left free for routing, fins per transistor, density and power-rail resistance — plus what you gain and lose against another height. The rail resistance it returns is what ir_drop consumes. Warns when the height does not land on the routing grid, which misaligns pins when alternate rows are flipped to share a rail. Idealised geometry: no real design rules, no vias, no parasitic extraction.

compareWithTracks.description: Compare against a cell of that height and return what is gained and lost

pitchNm.description: Routing-layer pitch: what one track is worth

rSheetOhmSq.description: Sheet resistance of the rail metal (ohm/square)

railTracks.description: Tracks consumed by BOTH rails together (VDD and VSS)

tracks.description: Height in routing tracks. Real libraries run ~6 to ~12; half tracks (7.5T) are legitimate

widthCpp.description: Cell width in CPP: an inverter is 2, a NAND2 is 3

name: standard_cell
